questions.sectionTitle: Section A: Multiple Choice Questions & Fundamentals
questions.prompt: In JavaScript/TypeScript event loops, which queue has strictly higher priority immediately after the current synchronous call stack clears?

options.text: `setInterval` preempts synchronous `for` loops
Microtask Queue (`Promise.then`, `queueMicrotask`, `MutationObserver`) runs completely before the next Macrotask (`setTimeout`)
Macrotask Queue (`setTimeout(fn, 0)`) always runs before resolved Promises
CSS Repaint callbacks execute mid-function before return statements

questions.explanation: The JS runtime drains every queued microtask after each synchronous turn before picking up a single macrotask from the task queue.

questions.prompt: What does `unknown` enforce in TypeScript compared to `any`?

options.text: `unknown` forbids calling methods or accessing properties until runtime type narrowing proves its shape; `any` disables type checking entirely
`unknown` strips properties during runtime JSON serialization
`any` performs stricter compile-time safety checks than `unknown`
`unknown` converts numbers to undefined automatically

questions.explanation: `unknown` is the type-safe top type for untrusted inputs (like JSON.parse), compelling explicit validation/narrowing.

questions.prompt: Why does JavaScript recommend strict equality (`===`) over loose equality (`==`)?

options.text: `==` does not work on objects or arrays at all
`===` mutates compared variables into constants
`==` executes asynchronously
`===` checks both value and type without surprising implicit type coercion (e.g., `0 == ''` is true, `0 === ''` is false)

questions.explanation: Strict equality avoids JS's complex abstract equality coercion rules.

questions.prompt: How does `Promise.allSettled()` differ from `Promise.all()`?

options.text: `Promise.allSettled()` waits for all promises to finish and returns each status (`fulfilled`/`rejected`); `Promise.all()` rejects immediately on the first error
`Promise.allSettled()` executes promises sequentially one by one
`Promise.all()` ignores rejected promises silently
They have identical error behavior

questions.explanation: `Promise.allSettled()` is ideal when independent batch requests shouldn't abort each other if one fails.

questions.prompt: Look at this TypeScript discriminated union handler. How can TS guarantee exhaustiveness at compile time if a new `status` case is added later?
questions.codeSnippet:
type State = { kind: 'ok'; data: string } | { kind: 'err'; error: Error };
function handle(s: State) { switch (s.kind) { case 'ok': return s.data; case 'err': return s.error.message; } }

options.text: Disable `strict` in `tsconfig.json`
Use `typeof s === 'object'`
Add a `default: const _exhaustive: never = s; return _exhaustive;` branch forcing compile errors on unhandled union cases
Cast `s as any` before switching

questions.explanation: Assigning unreachable `default` cases to `never` guarantees compile-time exhaustive checking when new union members are introduced.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Core Primitives and Syntax in TypeScript

questions.prompt: When fetching remote JSON safely in browser React code with proper error handling (`401`, `500`, network drops), what pattern prevents uncaught rejection crashes?
